children.text: kalaho vivādo 'dhikaraṇam kiṃmūlaṃ kuśalena ca /
children.translated_text: Quarrel, dispute, legal case — what is the root [of each]? And by one skilled [in Vinaya]—

children.text: syād vivādo anadhhikaraṇam vivādaṃ katibhiḥ śameta //
children.translated_text: how may a dispute arise that is not a legal case? By how many [methods] may a dispute be settled?

children.text: vivādaṃ saṃmukhaṃ śamayec chalākāgrahaṇena ca /
children.translated_text: A dispute should be settled face to face, and by the taking of lots (<s>śalākāgrahaṇa</s>);

children.text: anavavādaṃ saṃmukhaṃ smṛtyā amūḍhavinayena ca //
children.translated_text: by non-accusation (<s>anavavāda</s>), face-to-face [procedure], by recollection (<s>smṛti</s>), and by the discipline for one who has recovered sanity (<s>amūḍhavinaya</s>);

children.text: tathaiva tatsvabhāvaiṣīyaṃ tṛṇaprastārakeṇa ca /
children.translated_text: likewise by the procedure of ascertaining the true nature (<s>tatsvabhāvaiṣīya</s>), and by the covering with grass (<s>tṛṇaprastāraka</s>);

children.text: samagreṇa va saṃghena kṛtyādhikaraṇaṃ tathā //
children.translated_text: and by the entire <s>saṃgha</s> (community), the legal-act case (<s>kṛtyādhikaraṇa</s>) likewise

children.text: vyupaśamitavyam iti proktaṃ maharṣiṇā //
children.translated_text: should be pacified — thus spoke the great sage (<s>maharṣi</s>).

children.text:
The Buddha at Kapilavastu
King Śuddhodana listens to Buddha's sermons
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> at <s>Kapilavastu</s>. King <s>Śuddhodana</s> listens to the <s>Buddha</s>'s sermons.

children.text: buddho bhagavān kapilavastuni viharati nyāgrodhārāme; yadā bhagavatā śākyās satyeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitās tasā te trir bhagavantaṃ ḥdarśanāyaḥ upasaṃkramanti; teṣāṃ bhagavān abhīkṣṇaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati; ācaritam rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya śākyagaṇaparivṛtasya trir bhagavantaṃ ḥdarśanāyaḥ upasaṃkramitum; yāvad apareṇa samayena bhagavān anekaśatāyāḥ parṣadaḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaṃ deśayati kṣaudraṃ madhv ivāneḍakam; anekaśatā ca parṣad bhagavataḥ sakāśān (
Adhik-v 60
children.translated_text: Adhik-v 60

children.text: ) madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇoti āniñjyamānair indriyaiḥ; rājā śuddhodano mahatyā rājaṛddhyā mahatā rājānubhāvena śākyagaṇaparivṛto bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkrānto dharmaśravaṇāya; sa dharmaṃ śrutvā prakrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: exceedingly sweet, with senses unwavering. King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, with great royal splendor and great royal majesty, surrounded by the <s>Śākya</s> assembly, had approached the presence of the Blessed One to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, he departed.

The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One (<s>Bhagavān</s>), was dwelling at <s>Kapilavastu</s> in the <s>Nyagrodha</s> grove. After the Blessed One had established the <s>Śākyas</s> in the truths, they would approach the Blessed One three times for an audience. The Blessed One would teach them the <s>Dharma</s> repeatedly. It was the custom of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, surrounded by the <s>Śākya</s> assembly, to approach the Blessed One three times for an audience. Then on another occasion, the Blessed One, seated before an assembly of many hundreds, was teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, [sweet] like fine honey, pure and undefiled. And the assembly of many hundreds was listening to the <s>Dharma</s> from the Blessed One,

children.text: Queen Mahāprajāvatī asks king Śuddhodana to permit Śākya women to listen to the doctrine
children.translated_text: Queen <s>Mahāprajāvatī</s> asks King <s>Śuddhodana</s> to permit <s>Śākya</s> women to listen to the doctrine.

children.text: tato mahānāmā śākyo dharmaṃ śrutvā bhagavato 'ntike prasādajātaḥ svagṛhaṃ gataḥ kathayati: aho buddha aho dharma aho saṃgha saphalo 'smākaṃ buddhotpādaḥ iti; mahānāmno 'gramahiṣī kathayati: āryaputra, kim etat? sa kathayati: adya bhagavatā anekaśatāyāḥ parṣadaḥ purastād īdṛśī dharmo deśito yaṃ śrutvānekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasraiḥ mahān viśeṣo 'dhigataḥ iti; sā kathatati: āryaputra, yat kathayasi saphalo 'smākaṃ buddhotpāda iti satyam etat; saphala eva yuṣmākaṃ buddhotpādo nāsmākam; kiṃ kāraṇam? yasmāt puruṣāṇām arthāya bhagavān buddho loka utpanno na strīṇām; sa kathayati: bhadre, maivaṃ kathaya; sarvasatvahitānukampī bhagavān; gacchata yūyam api, bhagavato 'ntikād dharmaṃ śṛṇuta; sā kathayati: devaḥ śākyagaṇaparivṛtas trir bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmati; vayaṃ jihrema saṃmukhaṃ devasya purastād (
A 332b
children.translated_text: A 332b

children.text: ) dharmaṃ śrotum; tad yadi deva ekaṃ vāraṃ vāraṃ gacched pūrvāhṇārambhe vayam apy aparāhṇe bhagavato 'ntikād dharmaṃ śṛṇuyāmaḥ; mahānāmā śākyaḥ saṃlakṣayati: gacchāmi, devaṃ prabodhayāmi iti; punaḥ saṃlakṣayati: duḥkhaṃ svadārāṇām arthāya devo vijñāpyate; mahāprajāvatī devasya bahumatā; tasyāḥ śrotavyaṃ yat kartavyaṃ manyate; tasyā etam arthaṃ nivedayāmi iti; sa yena mahāprajāvatī gautamī tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ; upasaṃkramya mahāprajāvatyā (
children.translated_text: Therefore, if the king would go once during the forenoon, we too could hear the <s>Dharma</s> from the Blessed One in the afternoon.' The <s>Śākya</s> <s>Mahānāman</s> reflected: 'I shall go and inform the king.' Then he reflected again: 'It is difficult to petition the king for the sake of one's own wives. <s>Mahāprajāvatī</s> is highly esteemed by the king. Let her decide what should be heard and done. I shall convey this matter to her.' He approached <s>Mahāprajāvatī Gautamī</s>. Having approached, he conveyed this matter to <s>Mahāprajāvatī</s>

) gautamyā etam arthaṃ nivedayitavān; sā kathayati: evaṃ bhavatu, devaṃ prabodhayāmi iti; tato mahānamnā gṛhapatinā gṛhaṃ gatvā śākyāyanīnām ārocitam; tataḥ tāḥ śākyāyinyāḥ anyāś ca yena mahāprajāvatī gautamī tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ; upasaṃkramya mahāprajāvatīṃ gautamīm idam avocan: yat khalu gautami jānīyāḥ, śrutam asmābhir bhagavān anekaśatāyāḥ parṣadaḥ purastān madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ deśayati kṣaudram madhv ivāneḍakam, anekaśatā ca parṣad bhagavataḥ sakāśān madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇoti āniñjyamānair indriyaiḥ iti; tad icchāmo vayam api bhagavato 'ntikād dharmaṃ śrotum; asmākam arthaṃ devaṃ vijñāpaya yathā devaḥ pūrvāhṇe bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkrāmati vayam apy aparāhṇe; sā kathayati: bhaginyaḥ, śobhanaṃ yuṣmābhiś cittam utpāditam, tiṣṭhata muhūrtam yāvad rājānaṃ śuddhodanam avalokayāmi iti;
atha mahāprajāvatī gautamī yena rājā śuddhodanas tenopasaṃkrāntā; upasaṃkramya rājānaṃ śuddhodanam idam avocat; yat khalu deva jānīyāḥ, śrutaṃ mayā bhagavān anekaśatāyāḥ parṣadaḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo madhuramadhuraṃ dharmaṃ deśayati kṣaudraṃ madhv ivāneḍakam; anekaśatā ca parṣad bhagavato 'ntikād dharmaṃ śṛṇoti āniñjyamānair indriyair iti; śākyānikābhir apy evaṃ śrutam, ākāṃkṣanti dharmaṃ śrotum; tad arhasi deva pūrvāhṇe bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkramitum; aham api śākyānikā ādāya bhagavatsakāśam aparāhṇe upasaṃkramiṣyāmi; yat kāraṇam? tāḥ pūrvāhṇe gṛhavyāpāravyāpṛtāḥ na labhante ḥ'vakāśaṃḥ bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkramitum iti; ācaritaṃ rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya yadā mahāprajāvatī gautamī ājñāṃ dadāti uddaṇḍaśarīro 'vatiṣṭhate, tāvac ca rājā ḥnaḥ niṣīdati yāvan mahāprajāvatyā ājñādānam anuṣṭhitaṃ bhavati iti; sa praṇataśirā kathayati; gautani, enaṃ bhavatu iti(
children.translated_text: <s>Gautamī</s>. She said: 'So be it, I shall inform the king.' Then the householder <s>Mahānāman</s>, having gone home, informed the <s>Śākya</s> women. Then those <s>Śākya</s> women and others approached <s>Mahāprajāvatī Gautamī</s>. Having approached, they said to <s>Mahāprajāvatī Gautamī</s>: 'May <s>Gautamī</s> know this: we have heard that the Blessed One, seated before an assembly of many hundreds, teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, exceedingly sweet, like fine honey, pure and undefiled, and that an assembly of many hundreds hears the exceedingly sweet <s>Dharma</s> from the Blessed One with senses unwavering. We too wish to hear the <s>Dharma</s> from the Blessed One. Please petition the king on our behalf, so that the king may approach the Blessed One in the forenoon and we may [go] in the afternoon.' She said: 'Sisters, a noble thought has been generated by you. Wait a moment while I attend to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>.' Then <s>Mahāprajāvatī Gautamī</s> approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. Having approached, she said to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: 'May the king know this: I have heard that the Blessed One, seated before an assembly of many hundreds, teaches the exceedingly sweet <s>Dharma</s>, like fine honey, pure and undefiled; and that an assembly of many hundreds hears the <s>Dharma</s> from the Blessed One with senses unwavering. The <s>Śākya</s> women have also heard this and desire to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. May the king be pleased to approach the Blessed One in the forenoon. I too, taking the <s>Śākya</s> women, shall approach the Blessed One in the afternoon. Why? Because in the forenoon they are occupied with household duties and do not find the opportunity to approach the Blessed One.' It was the custom of King <s>Śuddhodana</s> that whenever <s>Mahāprajāvatī Gautamī</s> gave a command, he would stand with his body erect, and the king would not sit down until <s>Mahāprajāvatī</s>'s command had been carried out. With bowed head he said: '<s>Gautamī</s>, let it be so.'

Then the <s>Śākya</s> <s>Mahānāman</s>, having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, generated faith in the presence of the Blessed One. Having gone to his own house, he said: 'O <s>Buddha</s>! O <s>Dharma</s>! O <s>Saṃgha</s>! Fruitful for us is the arising of a <s>Buddha</s>!' <s>Mahānāman</s>'s chief queen said: 'Noble lord, what is this?' He said: 'Today the Blessed One has taught such a <s>Dharma</s> before an assembly of many hundreds that, having heard it, many hundreds of thousands of beings have attained a great distinction.' She said: 'Noble lord, what you say — that the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> is fruitful for us — is true; the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> is fruitful indeed for you, but not for us. Why? Because the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> has arisen in the world for the benefit of men, not of women.' He said: 'Good lady, do not speak thus! The Blessed One has compassion for the welfare of all beings. Go, you too, and hear the <s>Dharma</s> in the presence of the Blessed One.' She said: 'The king, surrounded by the <s>Śākya</s> assembly, approaches the Blessed One three times for an audience. We would be ashamed to hear the <s>Dharma</s> face to face, in the presence of the king.

Then <s>Mahāprajāvatī Gautamī</s>, surrounded by five hundred <s>Śākya</s> women, went to the <s>Nyagrodha</s> grove to hear the <s>Dharma</s> from the Blessed One. Now the wife of <s>Mahānāman</s> the <s>Śākya</s> went adorned with all ornaments. Beautiful, youthful, and adorned with all ornaments, she began to captivate the minds of those not free from passion. She was seen by the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, who said: 'Sister, you are naturally beautiful, good-looking, and graceful — how much more so when adorned with all ornaments! It is not proper that you have come wearing ornaments. These great souls

children.text: iti; atha bhagavata etad abhavat: iyaṃ rohikā dārikā pūrvabuddheṣu kṛtādhikārikā kiṃ tv alpāyuskā; uddhartavyā iyaṃ saṃsāracārakād iti viditvā ṛddhyā gāthaṃ bhūrjapatre ālikhya dattavān
children.translated_text: Thus. Then this thought occurred to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "This girl <s>Rohikā</s> has accumulated merit under former <s>Buddhas</s>, but she is short-lived. She must be rescued from the wandering in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence)." Knowing this, by his supernatural power he inscribed a verse on a birch-bark leaf and gave it to her:

children.text: utpannasya vināśaṃ hi jñātvā kālyāṇi janmani /
children.translated_text: "Having known, O virtuous one, the destruction of what has arisen in this birth,

children.text: yatnam āsthāya kalyāṇaṃ śrotavyaṃ mama bhāṣitam //
children.translated_text: you should listen with effort to my words, which are wholesome."

children.text: iti; atha rohikā dārikā hṛṣṭā tuṣṭā prītisaumanasyajātā gāthāṃ bhāṣate; buddhālambanenaiva cetasā saṃprasthitā
children.translated_text: Thus. Then the girl <s>Rohikā</s>, delighted, pleased, filled with joy and gladness, spoke a verse, having set forth with her mind fixed upon the <s>Buddha</s>:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇy api kalpaśatair api /
children.translated_text: "Deeds do not perish even after hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons);

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām //
children.translated_text: when they meet with the right conditions and the right time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings."

children.text: iti; alpāyuṣkāyāḥ karmaṇaḥ sāmagrī prāptā; gavā taruṇavatsayā jīvitād vyaparopitā; sā bhagavato 'ntike cittam abhiprasādya kālagatā
children.translated_text: Thus. For this short-lived girl, the conditions of her <s>karma</s> (deeds) were met. She was killed by a cow with a young calf. Having generated faith in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, she passed away.

The girl <s>Muktā</s> was entrusted to eight nurses — two shoulder-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses. She was raised and nurtured by the eight nurses with milk, curds, fresh butter, ghee, cream of ghee, and other specially prepared provisions, and she grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. Then, at another time, merchants from <s>Śrāvastī</s>, having equipped an ocean-going vessel, descended into the great ocean as traders. Having completed their voyage, they were carried by the wind to <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s>.
Then, having unloaded their merchandise, they settled not far from the royal palace. In the last watch of the night, at the time of dawn, they began to recite at length the <s>Udānas</s> (inspired utterances), <s>Pārāyaṇas</s> (chapters on the way beyond), <s>Satyadṛśas</s> (seers of truth), <s>Sthaviragāthās</s> (verses of the elders), <s>Sthavirīgāthās</s> (verses of the elder nuns), <s>Śailagāthās</s> (rock verses), <s>Munigāthās</s> (verses of the sage), and the <s>Arthavargīya</s> (chapter on purpose). <s>Muktikā</s>, from her position in the palace, heard them through the window. Then she reported to the king: "Your Majesty, merchants who have come from the Middle Country are singing beautifully." The king ordered his ministers: "Sirs, summon those singers." They were summoned. <s>Muktikā</s> said: "Let the gentlemen sing — let us hear what kind of music they have in the Middle Country." They replied: "Princess, we are not musicians. We are merchants from <s>Śrāvastī</s>, brought here by the wind. What we recited at the last watch of the night was the word of the <s>Buddha</s>." When <s>Muktikā</s> heard the sound "<s>Buddha</s>" — which she had never heard before — all the pores of her body bristled with excitement. Filled with curiosity, she asked: "Sirs, who is this one called <s>Buddha</s>?" children.translated_text: And she should be told thus: 'Venerable sir, what should be done by a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), that has been done by the Blessed One. Having relied on the Blessed One as a spiritual friend, I have been lifted up from the hells, animal births, and hungry ghosts; I have been established among gods and humans; I have brought <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) to its end; the oceans of blood and tears have been dried up; the mountains of bones have been crossed over; having split open the rock of the view of the perishable collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), accumulated since beginningless time, with the thunderbolt of knowledge, I have directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). I am, venerable sir, well advanced, well advanced! I go to the Blessed One for refuge, and to the <s>Dharma</s>, and to the community of monks (<s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s>). Remember me as a female lay disciple (<s>upāsikā</s>), from this day forward as long as I live, one with breath, one who has taken refuge, one who is devoted.' And take these three strings of pearls: one for the <s>Buddha</s>, one for the <s>Dharma</s>, one for the <s>Saṃgha</s>.' Then those merchants, taking the goods and the message, set out. In due course they arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Having rested from the fatigue of the journey, they approached the Blessed One. Having fallen at his feet and conveyed the message as instructed, they said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, these three strings of pearls have been sent by <s>Muktikā</s>: one for the <s>Buddha</s>, one for the <s>Dharma</s>, one for the <s>Saṃgha</s>.' The venerable <s>Ānanda</s> asked the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, from where has this gift arrived?' The Blessed One said: 'Did you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, the maid-servant of <s>Mahānāman</s> the <s>Śākya</s>, named <s>Rohikā</s>, who departed after hearing the <s>Dharma</s> from me? And on the road she was killed by a cow with a young calf?' 'I saw her, venerable sir.' 'She, having generated faith in my presence, died and was reborn as the daughter of the king of <s>Siṃhala</s> in <s>Siṃhaladvīpa</s> (Sri Lanka), named <s>Muktikā</s>. Having realized the truths, she has sent this gift. Therefore, the <s>Buddha</s>'s share should be used as plaster for the fragrant chamber (<s>gandhakuṭī</s>); the <s>Dharma</s>'s share should go to the individuals who bear the <s>Dharma</s>; and the <s>Saṃgha</s>'s share should be divided by the entire <s>Saṃgha</s>.' The monks (<s>bhikṣus</s>), having doubts, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, who cuts through all doubts: 'Venerable sir, what <s>karma</s> did <s>Muktikā</s> perform that she became a maid-servant? What <s>karma</s> did she perform that she was reborn in a wealthy royal family, and realized the truths?' The Blessed One said: 'Monks, the <s>karmas</s> were performed and accumulated by <s>Muktikā</s> herself — having gathered their provisions, with their conditions matured, standing before her like a flood, inevitable in their fruition. The <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated by <s>Muktikā</s> — who else would experience them? Monks, <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element. Rather, in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), <s>karmas</s> performed ripen — both wholesome and unwholesome.

children.translated_text: What is a procedural case? Whatever formal act (<s>karmajñapti</s>) of the <s>saṃgha</s> — a motion, a motion with a second resolution, or a motion with a fourth resolution — on account of which there is quarrel, dispute, contention, and controversy — this is called a procedural case.

The Blessed One said: 'That share of the <s>Dharma</s> belongs to persons who are preachers of the <s>Dharma</s>.' Therein, the <s>Sūtrāntikas</s> (those who hold to the discourses) say: 'We preserve the entire <s>sūtra</s> of the Blessed One; we are bearers of the <s>Dharma</s>; this gain accrues to us.' The bearers of the <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline) say: 'We are the guardians of the inner treasury of the Blessed One; we preserve the entire <s>Vinaya</s>; we are bearers of the <s>Dharma</s>; this gain accrues to us.' The bearers of the <s>Mātṛkā</s> (matrix texts) say: 'We preserve both the specific characteristics and the general characteristics of the <s>Sūtra</s> and the <s>Vinaya</s>; we are bearers of the <s>Dharma</s>; this gain accrues to us.' Therein, a quarrel, dispute, contention, and controversy arose among the bearers of the <s>Sūtra</s>, the bearers of the <s>Vinaya</s>, and the bearers of the <s>Mātṛkā</s>. Thereupon the Blessed One addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s>: '<s>Bhikṣus</s>, let there be no quarrel, no dispute, no contention, no controversy! There are, <s>bhikṣus</s>, four kinds of legal cases (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>). What are the four? A dispute case (<s>vivādādhikaraṇa</s>), an accusation case (<s>anavavādādhikaraṇa</s>), an offense case (<s>āpattyadhikaraṇa</s>), and a procedural case (<s>kṛtyādhikaraṇa</s>).
  What is a dispute case? When the <s>saṃgha</s> has different views, a dispute, opposing arguments, disagreement, discord, non-unity — on account of which there is quarrel, dispute, contention, and controversy — this is called a dispute case.
  What is an accusation case? When the <s>saṃgha</s> has an accusation, the making of an accusation, the initiation of an accusation — on account of which there is quarrel, dispute, contention, and controversy — this is called an accusation case.
  What is an offense case? There are five categories of offenses, called the aggregate of offenses. What five? <s>Pārājikas</s> (defeats), <s>saṃghāvaśeṣas</s> (offenses requiring formal meeting), <s>pāyattikas</s> (offenses requiring expiation), <s>pratideśanīyas</s> (offenses requiring confession), and <s>duṣkṛtas</s> (misdeeds) — on account of which there is quarrel, dispute, contention, and controversy — this is called an offense case.

Is a reproof (<s>anavavāda</s>) the same as a legal proceeding (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>), or is a legal proceeding the same as a reproof? He said: There may be a reproof that is not a legal proceeding; there may be a legal proceeding that is not a reproof; there may be both a reproof and a legal proceeding; there may be neither a reproof nor a legal proceeding. 1) A reproof that is not a legal proceeding: that which is the <s>saṃgha</s>'s reproof, the act of reproving, the initiation of a reproof. 2) A legal proceeding that is not a reproof: three [kinds of] legal proceedings — a dispute-proceeding (<s>vivādādhikaraṇa</s>), an offense-proceeding (<s>āpattyadhikaraṇa</s>), and a duties-proceeding (<s>kṛtyādhikaraṇa</s>). 3) Both a reproof and a legal proceeding: that which is the <s>saṃgha</s>'s reproof, the act of reproving, the initiation of a reproof — and on that basis whatever quarrel, contention, dispute, or disagreement [arises]. 4) Neither a reproof nor a legal proceeding: setting aside these cases.
Is an offense (<s>āpatti</s>) the same as a legal proceeding, or is a legal proceeding the same as an offense? He said: There may be an offense that is not a legal proceeding; there may be a legal proceeding that is not an offense; there may be both an offense and a legal proceeding; there may be neither an offense nor a legal proceeding. 1) An offense that is not a legal proceeding: the five classes of offenses, the categories of offenses, what are called the groups of offenses — <s>pārājikas</s>, <s>saṃghāvaśeṣas</s>, <s>pāyattikas</s>, <s>pratideśanikas</s>, and <s>duṣkṛtas</s>. 2) A legal proceeding that is not an offense: three [kinds of] legal proceedings — a dispute-proceeding, a reproof-proceeding (<s>anavavādādhikaraṇa</s>), and a duties-proceeding. 3) Both an offense and a legal proceeding: the five classes of offenses, the categories of offenses, what are called the groups of offenses — <s>pārājikas</s>, <s>saṃghāvaśeṣas</s>, <s>pāyattikas</s>, <s>pratideśanikas</s>, and <s>duṣkṛtas</s> — and on that basis

Is every dispute a legal case, and is every legal case a dispute? [The answer] is said: There may be a dispute that is not a legal case; there may be a legal case that is not a dispute; there may be both a dispute and a legal case; and there may be neither a dispute nor a legal case. 1) A dispute that is not a legal case: when the <s>saṃgha</s> has different views, a dispute, and opposing arguments [without the formal elements of a legal case]. 2) A legal case that is not a dispute: three legal cases — the accusation case, the offense case, and the procedural case. 3) Both a dispute and a legal case: when the <s>saṃgha</s> has different views, a dispute, opposing arguments, disagreement, discord, non-unity — on account of which there is quarrel, dispute, contention, and controversy. 4) Neither a dispute nor a legal case: setting aside these aspects.

Monks, by how many principles for the settlement of legal proceedings (<s>adhikaraṇaśamatha dharma</s>) should a dispute-proceeding be controlled, settled, and fully resolved? He said: By two — by face-to-face resolution (<s>saṃmukhavinaya</s>) and by majority vote (<s>yadbhūyasikīya śalākāgrahaṇa</s>). How does face-to-face resolution serve as a principle for settlement of legal proceedings, and how does it bring about the control, settlement, and full resolution of these legal proceedings?
The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> for the rains retreat, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, a number of monks had entered the rains retreat in the countryside. During their retreat, a quarrel, contention, dispute, and disagreement arose among them. They entrusted that legal proceeding to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>. Those two resolved that legal proceeding in accordance with <s>Dharma</s>, with <s>Vinaya</s>, and with the Teacher's instruction. Then those many monks, having completed the rains retreat in the countryside, after three months had passed, having made their robes and completed their robes, taking up their bowls and robes, set out on a wandering tour toward <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Wandering by stages, they arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Then those many monks, having put away their bowls and robes and washed their feet, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Now it is the nature of <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, to greet visiting monks with this greeting: 'From where have you monks now come, and where did you spend the rains?' The Blessed One greeted those many monks: 'From where have you, monks, now come, and where did you spend the rains?' 'From the countryside, venerable sir, we have now come, and we spent the rains in the countryside.' 'I trust, monks, that you spent the rains comfortably in the countryside and were not fatigued by [the search for] alms-food?' 'Indeed, venerable sir, we did spend the rains comfortably in the countryside and were not fatigued by alms-food. However, during our retreat a quarrel, contention, dispute, and disagreement arose among us. We entrusted that legal proceeding to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>.

This is a mediator (<s>sthalastha</s>) restrained in body but not in speech. What is a mediator restrained both in body and in speech? A mediator among <s>bhikṣus</s> who have quarreled, entered into dispute, taken opposing sides — to one side he does not approach in person nor send a messenger; to the second side also he does not approach in person nor send a messenger. children.translated_text: The simple face-to-face [procedure] (<s>śuddhakaṃ saṃmukham</s>). What is 'face-to-face' here? By whichever <s>Dharma</s>, by whichever <s>Vinaya</s>, by whichever instruction of the Teacher that legal case is settled — by that <s>Dharma</s>, by that <s>Vinaya</s>, by that instruction of the Teacher they settle that legal case. The <s>saṃgha</s> should settle that legal case according to the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Vinaya</s>, and the Teacher's instruction. When the <s>saṃgha</s> has settled that legal case according to the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Vinaya</s>, and the Teacher's instruction, it is well-settled.

I, the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so, the legal case conveyor, now deposit this legal case with the <s>bhikṣus</s> who are bearers of the <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>Mātṛkā</s>. That legal case should be settled by the <s>bhikṣus</s> who are bearers of the <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>Mātṛkā</s> — in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Vinaya</s>, and the teaching of the Teacher. By the <s>bhikṣus</s> who are bearers of the <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>Mātṛkā</s>, that legal case should be declared settled and well settled.

The pure <s>saṃmukha</s> (presence): What is the presence here? There are three presences: <s>saṃgha-saṃmukha</s> (presence of the community), <s>pudgala-saṃmukha</s> (presence of the person), and <s>dharma-saṃmukha</s> (presence of the teaching). What is <s>saṃgha-saṃmukha</s>? As many <s>bhikṣus</s> as have arrived within the <s>sīmā</s> (boundary) and are entitled to participate in the act (<s>kriyā-prāpta</s>), all are attentive and present; the consent (<s>chanda</s>) has been brought from those entitled to give consent; and the attentive, present <s>bhikṣus</s> do not object and do not protest; for those who object and protest, the protest is upheld, and the formal acts (<s>karmāṇi</s>) are performed — this is called <s>saṃgha-saṃmukha</s>. What is <s>pudgala-saṃmukha</s>? Those who settle that legal case and those whose legal case is being settled are all attentive and present — this is called <s>pudgala-saṃmukha</s>. What is <s>dharma-saṃmukha</s>? By whatever <s>Dharma</s>, by whatever <s>Vinaya</s>, by whatever instruction of the <s>Śāstṛ</s> that legal case is settled, by that <s>Dharma</s>, by that <s>Vinaya</s>, by that instruction of the <s>Śāstṛ</s> they settle that legal case — this is called <s>dharma-saṃmukha</s>. If the <s>Saṃgha</s> which includes its elders (<s>sa-sthavira</s>) and possesses the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> is unable to settle that legal case, it should refer that legal case to the <s>adhikaraṇa-saṃcāraka</s> <s>bhikṣu</s> himself; the <s>adhikaraṇa-saṃcāraka</s> <s>bhikṣu</s> should refer it to <s>bhikṣus</s> who are bearers of the <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>Mātṛkā</s> (matrices); and he should report it as it occurred: 'Let the venerable <s>bhikṣus</s> who are bearers of the <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>Mātṛkā</s> hear:

children.text: śuddhakaṃ saṃmukham; kim atra saṃmukham? dve saṃmukhe pudgalasaṃmukhaṃ dharmasaṃmukhaṃ ca; pudgalasaṃmukham katamat? ye tad adhikaraṇaṃ vyupaśamayanti yeṣāṃ ca tad adhikaraṇaṃ vyupaśāmyati te sarve samavahitā bhavanti saṃmukhībhūtāḥ; idam ucyate pudgalasaṃmukham; dharmasaṃmukhaṃ katamat? yena dharmeṇa yena vinayena yena śāstuḥ śāsanena tad adhikaraṇaṃ vyupaśāmyati tena dharmeṇa tena vinayena tena śāstuḥ śāsanena tad adhikaraṇaṃ vyupaśamayanti, idam ucyate dharmasaṃmukham; sacet sūtravinayamātṛkādharā bhikṣavo na śaknuvanti tad adhikaraṇam vyupaśamayituṃ tair adhikaraṇasaṃcārakasyaiva bhikṣor upanikṣeptavyam; adhikaraṇasaṃcārakeṇa bhikṣuṇā yasminn āvāse bhikṣuḥ sthavirasthavirānyatamaḥ pramukhaḥ pramukhānyatamaḥ jñāto jñātānyatamaḥ tasyopanikṣeptavyam; yathāvṛttaṃ cārocayitavyam, śṛṇu tvaṃ sthavira idam adhikaraṇam amuṣminn āvāse iyaccirakālasamutpannam asminn eva vastuni; tad adhikaraṇaṃ sthalasthair bhikṣubhir na śaktaṃ vyupaśamayitum; taiḥ saṃghe upanikṣiptam; saṃghenāpi na śaktam; tenāpi vyūḍhakā bhikṣavaḥ saṃmatāḥ; vyūḍhakair api bhikṣubhir na śaktam; tair api vyūḍhakavyūḍhakā bhikṣavaḥ saṃmatāḥ; vyūḍhakavyūḍhakair api bhikṣubhir na śaktam; saṃghe upanikṣiptam; saṃghenāpi aham evaṃnāmā adhikaraṇasaṃcārako bhikṣuḥ saṃmataḥ; saṃghe (

by me, the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so, the legal case conveyor, this legal case was deposited with the <s>saṃgha</s> together with its elders and <s>Prātimokṣa</s>. By the <s>saṃgha</s> together with its elders and <s>Prātimokṣa</s>, it could not be settled. By them too, it was deposited with me, the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so, the legal case conveyor. By me, the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so, the legal case conveyor, that legal case was deposited with the <s>bhikṣus</s> who are bearers of the <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>Mātṛkā</s>. By them too it could not [be settled]. By them too it was deposited with me, the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so, the legal case conveyor.
I, the <s>bhikṣu</s> named so-and-so, the legal case conveyor, now deposit this legal case with the elder. May the elder settle this legal case within the final limit. I shall prescribe the rules of proper conduct (<s>āsamudācārika dharma</s>) for the elder <s>bhikṣu</s>: by the elder <s>bhikṣu</s>, from the litigant and respondent <s>bhikṣus</s>, neither tooth-sticks nor cow-dung offerings nor bowl-offerings should be accepted, nor should recitation practice or questioning sessions be given, nor [should he sit] before or behind [either party]. They should be told: 'Venerable ones, let there be no quarrel, no dispute, no contention, no controversy! For what reason? There is no victory for two who are disputing, venerable ones; rather, there is victory for one and defeat for the other. There is no victory for two who are fighting; rather, there is victory for one and defeat for the other.' By the elder <s>bhikṣu</s>, that legal case should be settled in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Vinaya</s>, and the teaching of the Teacher. By the elder <s>bhikṣu</s>, that legal case should be declared settled and well settled. Thus, <s>bhikṣus</s>, the face-to-face <s>Vinaya</s> (<s>saṃmukhavinaya</s>) is a method for settling legal cases. And thus for certain legal cases there is taming, pacification, and complete settlement through the settlement method of the face-to-face <s>Vinaya</s>.

The pure face-to-face [procedure] (<s>śuddhakaṃ saṃmukha</s>). What is 'face to face' here? There are two kinds of 'face to face': face to face with persons (<s>pudgalasaṃmukha</s>) and face to face with the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmasaṃmukha</s>). What is face to face with persons? Those who settle that legal case and those whose legal case is settled — all of them are present and face to face. This is called face to face with persons. What is face to face with the <s>Dharma</s>? By whatever <s>Dharma</s>, whatever <s>Vinaya</s>, whatever teaching of the Teacher that legal case is settled — by that <s>Dharma</s>, by that <s>Vinaya</s>, by that teaching of the Teacher they settle that legal case. This is called face to face with the <s>Dharma</s>. If the <s>bhikṣus</s> who are bearers of the <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>Mātṛkā</s> are unable to settle that legal case, they should deposit it with the legal case conveyor <s>bhikṣu</s> himself. The legal case conveyor <s>bhikṣu</s> should deposit it with whatever <s>bhikṣu</s> in whatever monastery is an elder or one of the elders, a leader or one of the leaders, well-known or one of the well-known. And the circumstances should be reported: 'Listen, elder: this legal case arose in such-and-such a monastery, for such a long time, on this very matter. That legal case could not be settled by the <s>bhikṣus</s> on the spot. It was deposited with the <s>saṃgha</s>. By the <s>saṃgha</s> too it could not [be settled]. By them, investigator <s>bhikṣus</s> (<s>vyūḍhaka</s>) were appointed. By the investigator <s>bhikṣus</s> too it could not [be settled]. By them, re-investigators (<s>vyūḍhakavyūḍhaka</s>) were appointed. By the re-investigators too it could not [be settled]. It was deposited with the <s>saṃgha</s>. By five conditions, the taking of lots by majority as a settlement method becomes harsh, fierce, intense, suspicious of schism, and of irreversible application. How does it become harsh? It is harshly seized upon by the litigant and respondent <s>bhikṣus</s> — thus it becomes harsh. How does it become fierce? When any one of the fourteen matters that cause schism is well and properly grasped — thus it becomes suspicious of schism. How does it become of irreversible application? Beginning with those on the spot up to the elder — thus it becomes of irreversible application. Endowed with these five qualities, the settlement by taking lots by majority becomes harsh, fierce, intense, suspicious of schism, and of irreversible application. Then a lot-distributor <s>bhikṣu</s> (<s>śalākācāraka</s>) should be appointed. A lot-distributor <s>bhikṣu</s> endowed with five qualities should not be appointed if unappointed, and if appointed should be dismissed. What five? He goes by partiality, he goes by aversion, by delusion, by fear, and he does not know whether lots have been distributed or not. A lot-distributor <s>bhikṣu</s> endowed with these five qualities should not be appointed if unappointed, and if appointed should be dismissed. But a lot-distributor <s>bhikṣu</s> endowed with five [opposite] qualities should be appointed if unappointed, and if appointed should not be dismissed. What five? He does not go by partiality, not by aversion, not by delusion, not by fear, and he knows whether lots have been distributed or not. A lot-distributor <s>bhikṣu</s> endowed with these five qualities should be appointed if unappointed, and if appointed should not be dismissed.

What is the open distribution of voting tickets? For example, a ticket-distributing monk thinks: 'In this dwelling there are many senior monks who advocate <s>Dharma</s>, but few junior monks who advocate what is not <s>Dharma</s>. If I were to distribute the tickets secretly, it is possible that the junior monks would take the non-<s>Dharma</s> ticket. I should distribute the tickets openly. When distributing openly, it is possible that the junior monks, deferring to the senior monks, would take the <s>Dharma</s> ticket in large numbers.' He distributes the tickets openly. This is called the open distribution of voting tickets. What is the by-the-ear whispering distribution of voting tickets? For example, a ticket-distributing monk goes to [each monk's] ear and whispers: 'Venerable one, your preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>) has taken the <s>Dharma</s> ticket; you too should take the <s>Dharma</s> ticket. Your teacher (<s>ācārya</s>), your co-preceptor, your co-teacher, your friend, your intimate, your companion, your dear one has taken the <s>Dharma</s> ticket; you too should take the <s>Dharma</s> ticket.' This is called the by-the-ear whispering distribution of voting tickets. What is the full-<s>saṃgha</s> distribution of voting tickets? For example, a ticket-distributing monk thinks: 'In this dwelling many monks are ill. If I were to distribute the tickets when the full <s>saṃgha</s> is not assembled and not gathered, it is possible that many monks would take the non-<s>Dharma</s> ticket. I should rather distribute the tickets when the full <s>saṃgha</s> is assembled and gathered.' He distributes the tickets when the full <s>saṃgha</s> is assembled and gathered.
This is called the full-<s>saṃgha</s> distribution of voting tickets.

What is the secret distribution of voting tickets? For example, a ticket-distributing monk thinks: 'In this very dwelling there are many senior monks who advocate what is not <s>Dharma</s>, but few junior monks who advocate <s>Dharma</s>. If I were to distribute the tickets openly, it is possible that the junior monks, deferring to the senior monks, would take the non-<s>Dharma</s> ticket in large numbers. I should therefore distribute the tickets secretly.' He distributes the tickets secretly. This is called the secret distribution of voting tickets.

Beginning from those standing on the ground up to the <s>sthavira</s> (elder); thus they take the voting sticks without reversed procedure; How do they take the voting sticks with guidance of guides and leaders? Those <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) who are bearers of the <s>sūtra</s> (discourses), bearers of the <s>vinaya</s> (discipline), and bearers of the <s>mātṛkā</s> (matrices) — these are called the guides in that <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>; looking to these leaders, they take the voting sticks; thus they take the voting sticks precisely with the guidance of guides and leaders; How do they take the voting sticks thinking 'the <s>saṃgha</s> (community) will not be split by this taking of voting sticks'? children.translated_text: the non-confusion procedure (<s>amūḍhavinaya</s>) for the afflicted (<s>sekata</s>) monk. Or any other [case] of this kind — it should be given thus. Having arranged seats, sounding the gong, having made inquiry by roll-call, when the entire <s>saṃgha</s> is assembled and gathered, the afflicted monk, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having performed respectful salutation to the seniors, and standing in a crouching position, should say this: 'Let the venerable <s>saṃgha</s> hear me. I, the afflicted monk, being naked, deranged, with disturbed mind, and overcome by painful feelings, have committed many acts unworthy of a renunciant and contrary to the rules; I have spoken [improperly] and acted violently; saliva was discharged, the eyes were rolled, the face was contorted; though not sleeping, I was thought to be sleeping; though I had not spoken, others thought I had spoken. But at a later time I regained my own mind. Monks are accusing me on account of that matter. Being accused on account of that matter, I request the <s>saṃgha</s> for the non-confusion procedure. May the venerable <s>saṃgha</s> grant me, the afflicted monk, the non-confusion procedure, out of compassion.' Thus a second time, thus a third time. Thereafter, one monk should make a motion (<s>jñapti</s>) and the formal act (<s>karma</s>) should be performed: 'Let the venerable <s>saṃgha</s> hear. This afflicted monk, being naked, deranged, with disturbed mind, and overcome by painful feelings, has committed many acts unworthy of a renunciant and contrary to the rules; he has spoken [improperly] and acted violently; saliva was discharged, the eyes were rolled, the face was contorted; though not sleeping, he was thought to be sleeping; though he had not spoken, others thought he had spoken. But at a later time he regained his own mind. Monks are accusing him on account of that matter. Being accused on account of that matter, he requests the <s>saṃgha</s> for the non-confusion procedure. If it is the appropriate time for the <s>saṃgha</s> and it is agreeable and the <s>saṃgha</s> approves, may the <s>saṃgha</s> grant the afflicted monk the non-confusion procedure' — this is the motion. The formal act should be performed: 'Let the venerable <s>saṃgha</s> hear. This afflicted monk, being naked, deranged, with disturbed mind, and overcome by painful feelings, has committed many acts unworthy of a renunciant and contrary to the rules; he has spoken [improperly] and acted violently; saliva was discharged, the eyes were rolled, the face was contorted; though not sleeping, he was thought to be sleeping; though he had not spoken, others thought he had spoken. But at a later time he regained his own mind. Monks are accusing him on account of that matter. Being accused on account of that matter, he requests the <s>saṃgha</s> for the non-confusion procedure. The <s>saṃgha</s> grants the afflicted monk the non-confusion procedure. If the venerable ones approve of granting the afflicted monk the non-confusion procedure, let them remain silent; if they do not approve, let them speak. This is the first proclamation. Thus the second and third proclamations should be made.' The <s>saṃgha</s> has granted the afflicted monk the non-confusion procedure. The <s>saṃgha</s> has approved and consented, since it remained silent. Thus I retain it.

children.translated_text: Whether accused or not accused, whether reminded or not reminded, standing before a monk, he says thus: 'Please attend, venerable one. I, named so-and-so, have committed such-and-such an offense. I confess it and make it manifest before the venerable one. Having confessed and made it manifest, I shall be at ease, not having not confessed and not having not made it manifest.' [The other monk] should say: 'Do you see the offense?' He too should say: 'I see it.' The first should say: 'Will you undertake restraint in the future?' The latter should say: 'I shall undertake it.' This is the confession.

Monks, the offense-proceeding (<s>āpattyadhikaraṇa</s>) should be controlled, settled, and fully resolved by four principles for the settlement of legal proceedings. Which four? The confession procedure (<s>pratijñākāraka</s>), face-to-face resolution (<s>saṃmukhavinaya</s>), the investigation-of-own-nature procedure (<s>tatsvabhāvaiṣīya</s>), and the covering-with-grass procedure (<s>tṛṇaprastāraka</s>). How, monks, does the confession procedure serve as a principle for settlement of legal proceedings? And how does it bring about the control, settlement, and full resolution of certain legal proceedings, namely through the confession procedure? For example, a monk has committed an offense.

children.translated_text: Still others said: 'The Blessed One is the lord of the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Sugata</s> is the lord of the <s>Dharma</s> — by whomever he was suspended, he has been legitimately suspended [or not].' They gradually arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, put away their bowls and robes, washed their feet, and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, having bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, they sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the <s>bhikṣus</s> of <s>Vaiśālī</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Blessed One, the venerable <s>Kāla Mṛgāraputra</s> was suspended by us. Has the Blessed One suspended him or reinstated him?' The Blessed One said: '<s>Bhikṣus</s>, <s>Kāla Mṛgāraputra</s> was not rightly suspended by the <s>Dharma</s>. <s>Kāla Mṛgāraputra</s> is guiltless and has done no wrong. I have reinstated the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Kāla Mṛgāraputra</s>.' He asked: 'But why, <s>bhikṣus</s>, did you perform the act of suspension against a guiltless <s>bhikṣu</s>?'

The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s> in the <s>Jetavana</s> grove, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. At that time, the venerable <s>Kāla Mṛgāraputra</s> was dwelling at <s>Vaiśālī</s>, on the bank of the Monkey Pond, in the gabled hall. Through his presence, the <s>Licchavi</s> people of <s>Vaiśālī</s> were performing great services to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>. The <s>bhikṣus</s> of <s>Vaiśālī</s> observed: 'The venerable <s>Kāla Mṛgāraputra</s> was born elsewhere, grew up elsewhere — he was born in <s>Śrāvastī</s>. And the <s>Licchavi</s> people of <s>Vaiśālī</s> are exceedingly devoted [to him]. Therefore, the act of suspension (<s>utkṣepaṇīya karma</s>) should be performed against him so that the <s>Licchavi</s> people of <s>Vaiśālī</s> will not have faith [in him].' They began watching for an opportunity. Then a certain householder invited the <s>bhikṣu saṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> for bathing in a bathhouse. The <s>bhikṣus</s>, having placed their robes in the dressing room, began to bathe. But the venerable <s>Kāla Mṛgāraputra</s>, being mindful, placed his robes apart and began to bathe. Another <s>bhikṣu</s> too placed his robes in that very spot. Then the venerable <s>Kāla Mṛgāraputra</s>, having bathed, thinking 'these are my own robes,' put on the robes belonging to that [other] <s>bhikṣu</s> and departed. Then that <s>bhikṣu</s> arose and did not see his own robes. He began asking the <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'Venerable ones, who has taken my robes?' The Blessed One observed: 'My disciples indeed desire to settle legal cases as they arise — that is, in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Vinaya</s>, and the teaching of the Teacher.' Having understood this, he addressed the <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'How, <s>bhikṣus</s>, is the face-to-face <s>Vinaya</s> a method for settling legal cases? ihaikeṣām adhikaraṇānāṃ damaś ca bhavati śamaś ca vyupaśamaś ca yaduta tatsvabhāvaiṣīyena adhikaraṇaśamathena? iha hastako bhikṣuḥ saṃghamadhye āpattim avajānāti; avajñāya pratijānāti, pratijñāya punar apy ajānāti; etat prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti; bhagavān āha: dadata yūyaṃ bhikṣavo hastakasya bhikṣoḥ tatsvabhāviṣīyam iti yo vā punar anyo 'py evaṃjātīyaḥ evaṃ ca punar dātavyaḥ; śayanāsanaprajñaptiṃ kṛtvā gaṇḍīm ākoṭya pṛṣṭhavācikayā bhikṣūn samanuyujya sarvasaṃghe saṃniṣaṇṇe saṃnipatite ḥhastakena bhikṣuṇā ekāṃśam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yathāvṛddhikayā sāmīcīṃ kṛtvā utkuṭukena sthitvā idaṃ syād vacanīyam: śṛṇotu bhadantāḥ saṃgho, mayā hastakena bhikṣuṇā saṃghamadhye āpattir avajñātaḥ, avajñāya pratijñātaḥ, pratijñāya punar apy avajñātaḥ; so 'haṃ saṃghāt tatsvabhāvaiṣīyaṃ yāce, dadatu bhadantāḥ saṃgho me hastakasya bhikṣos tatsvabhāvaiṣīyam anukampām upādāya; evaṃ dvir apy evaṃ trir api; tataḥ paścād ekena bhikṣuṇā jñaptiṃ kṛtvā karma kartavyam; śṛṇotu bhadantāḥ saṃghaḥ, ayaṃ hastako bhikṣuḥ saṃghamadhye āpattim avajānāti avajñāya pratijānāti (

This <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Hastaka</s> requests the <s>saṃgha</s> for the <s>tatsvabhāvaiṣīya</s>. The <s>saṃgha</s> grants the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Hastaka</s> the <s>tatsvabhāvaiṣīya</s>. Those venerable ones who approve of granting the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Hastaka</s> the <s>tatsvabhāvaiṣīya</s>, let them remain silent; those who do not approve, let them speak.' This is the first proclamation (<s>karmavācanā</s>). Thus the second and third proclamations should be made. The <s>saṃgha</s> has granted the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Hastaka</s> the <s>tatsvabhāvaiṣīya</s>. The <s>saṃgha</s> has approved and consented, since it remained silent. Thus I retain it.
I shall prescribe the rules of proper conduct (<s>āsamudācārika dharma</s>) for the <s>bhikṣu</s> who has been given the <s>tatsvabhāvaiṣīya</s>. The <s>bhikṣu</s> who has been given the <s>tatsvabhāvaiṣīya</s> should not grant ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s>), should not confer full ordination (<s>upasaṃpadā</s>), should not give dependence (<s>niśraya</s>), should not appoint a novice (<s>śramaṇoddeśa</s>), should not perform formal acts, should not be appointed to conduct formal acts, should not admonish <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, should not be appointed as an admonisher of <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, should not admonish <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> even if previously appointed, should not reprove or remind a <s>bhikṣu</s> on account of moral failure, wrong view, conduct failure, or livelihood failure, should not raise a charge, should not [participate] in the <s>poṣadha</s>, the <s>pravāraṇā</s>, in formal acts requiring two proclamations (<s>jñaptidvitīya</s>) or four proclamations (<s>jñapticaturtha</s>); nor should he propound the <s>Vinaya</s> in the midst of the <s>saṃgha</s> when there are other persons who are bearers of the <s>Vinaya</s>. If the <s>bhikṣu</s> who has been given the <s>tatsvabhāvaiṣīya</s> fails to observe the prescribed rules of proper conduct, he incurs an offense (<s>sātisāra</s>).
There is one unlawful granting of the <s>tatsvabhāvaiṣīya</s> and one lawful. Which is the one unlawful? For example, the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Hastaka</s> confesses an offense in the midst of the <s>saṃgha</s>; having confessed, he denies; having denied, he again confesses — and the <s>saṃgha</s> grants him the <s>tatsvabhāvaiṣīya</s>. This is the unlawful granting of the <s>tatsvabhāvaiṣīya</s>. This is the one unlawful. Which is the one lawful? For example, the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Hastaka</s> denies an offense in the midst of the <s>saṃgha</s>; having denied it, he confesses; having confessed, he again denies — and the <s>saṃgha</s>

children.translated_text: The settling of legal cases by the <s>tṛṇaprastāraka</s> (covering-with-grass) method.

children.text: kathaṃ ca bhikṣavaḥ tṛṇaprastāraka adhikaraṇaśamatho bhavati? kathaṃ ca punar ihaikeṣām adhikaraṇānāṃ damaś ca bhavati śamaś ca ḥvyupaśamaśḥ yaduta tṛṇaprastārakeṇādhikaraṇaśamathena? yathāpitad bhikṣūṇāṃ kalahajātānāṃ viharatāṃ bhaṇḍanajātānāṃ vigṛhītānāṃ vivādam āpannānāṃ pakṣāparapakṣavyavasthitānām; ekasmin pakṣe yo bhikṣuḥ (

children.text: ) sthaviraḥ sthavirānyatamaḥ jñāto jñātānyatamaḥ pramukaḥ pramukhānyatamaḥ tena svapakṣe upasaṃkramya idaṃ syād vacanīyam: teṣām asmākam āyuṣmantaḥ alābhā na lābhāḥ durlabdhā na sulabdhāḥ, ye vayaṃ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajya kalahajātā viharāmo bhaṇḍanajātā vigṛhītā vivādam āpannāḥ; yāṃ cāham āyuṣmanto 'smin vastuni āpattim āpanno yāṃ ca yūyam, sthāpayitvā sthūlāvadyaṃ vā gṛhasthapratiśaraṇaṃ vā, utsahe 'ham ātmanaḥ karaṇīyena yuṣmākāṃ ca teṣām āyuṣmatām antike deśayitum āviṣkartuṃ na praticchādayitum iti; sacet tasya bhikṣoḥ svapakṣād ekabhikṣur api bhāṣitaṃ na prativahati na pratikrośati, tatas tena bhikṣuṇā dvitīyaṃ pakṣam upasaṃkramyaikāṃśam uttarāsaṅgam kṛtvā yathāvṛddhikayā sāmīcīṃ kṛtvā utkuṭukena sthitvā idaṃ syād vacanīyam: teṣām asmākam āyuṣmanta alābhā na lābhāḥ durlabdhā na sulabdhāḥ, ye vayam svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajya kalahajātā viharāmo bhaṇḍanajātā vigṛhītā vivādam āpannāḥ; yāṃ cāham asmin vastuny āpattim āpanno yāṃ ca te āyuṣmantaḥ, sthāpayitvā sthūlāvadyaṃ vā gṛhapatipratiśaraṇaṃ (
children.translated_text: A monk who is a senior, or one of the seniors, well-known or one of the well-known, prominent or one of the prominent — he should approach his own faction and say this: 'It is our loss, venerable ones, not our gain; it is our misfortune, not our good fortune, that we, having gone forth in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, dwell in a state of quarrel, contention, dispute, and disagreement. Whatever offense I have committed in this matter, and whatever offenses you have committed — setting aside gross offenses and those involving recourse to laypeople — I am willing to confess by what is proper for me and make manifest before you, venerable ones, and before those venerable ones, and not to conceal [them].' If not even one monk of his own faction objects to or protests against what was said, then that monk should approach the second faction, and having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, having performed respectful salutation to the seniors, and standing in a crouching position, should say this: 'It is our loss, venerable ones, not our gain; it is our misfortune, not our good fortune, that we, having gone forth in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, dwell in a state of quarrel, contention, dispute, and disagreement. And thus for certain legal proceedings there is control, settlement, and full resolution, namely through the covering-with-grass principle for settlement of legal proceedings.
The offense-proceeding (<s>āpattyadhikaraṇa</s>), monks, should be controlled, settled, and fully resolved by these four principles for the settlement of legal proceedings, namely: the confession procedure (<s>pratijñākāraka</s>), face-to-face resolution (<s>saṃmukhavinaya</s>), the investigation-of-own-nature procedure (<s>tatsvabhāvaiṣīya</s>), and the covering-with-grass procedure (<s>tṛṇaprastāraka</s>). The duties-proceeding (<s>kṛtyādhikaraṇa</s>), monks, should be resolved by the <s>saṃgha</s> in harmony.
